name: logo-wide-wordmark
story: A designer drew a channel bug in the top-right corner with a wide wordmark logo filling a rounded plate, an amber edge accent, and a strand text line below it, and exported the transparent frame as SVG.
idioms: the placed wide logo is a pattern-filled shape: <rect id="Logo plate" fill="url(#pattern0_88_504)"/>, not a positioned <image>
<pattern id="pattern0_88_504" patternContentUnits="objectBoundingBox" width="1" height="1"> holding <use xlink:href="#image0_88_504" transform="scale(0.5)">
the actual <image> carrying the base64 data: URI is parked last inside <defs>, with width/height and xlink:href
the layer name stays on the visible rect (id="Logo plate"); the <image> in defs is called image0_88_504
frame with no fill exports with fill="none" on the root and no backplate rect - transparent over live video
no <?xml?> prolog, zero indentation, uppercase hex (#F6A623), xml:space="preserve" plus style="white-space: pre" on text, letter-spacing in em
outer <g clip-path="url(#clip0_88_504)"> with matching <clipPath> rect in <defs>
whyThisMatters: A wide wordmark logo is an extreme aspect ratio (520x120) placed into a channel bug slot. Measuring this shape tests whether the importer recognizes Figma's pattern-filled rectangle as a swappable picture field when the aspect is strongly horizontal, and verifies that a channel bug's fixed corner layout defaults to shrink rather than stretching the logo plate when strand copy varies.
